cardiogenic-shock-fixtures.ts binds seed 4390 and content 0.1.0 to expert, bridge-before-the-heart error, recovery, and no-action paths. The acute anterior STEMI pattern deteriorating while the catheterization pathway is mobilised, the invasive 78/48 mmHg at a MAP of 58 with HR 112/min in sinus, cool mottled extremities, capillary refill 5 seconds, new confusion, 10 mL of urine in the last hour and a lactate rising from 3.1 to 4.8 mmol/L, the 91% on supplemental oxygen at RR 28/min with bilateral crackles, the fixed ECG reporting persistent anterior ST elevation, and the fixed echo reporting severe left-ventricular systolic dysfunction with anterior and apical akinesis, a preserved right ventricle, no effusion, no reported acute severe mitral regurgitation or ventricular-septal defect and bilateral B-lines are authored constants; no haemodynamic, vasopressor or reperfusion model is claimed, and no outcome follows from any choice. tests/integration/cardiogenic-shock-runs.test.ts replays every path frame-for-frame across all three guidance levels and both practice regions.

The shared audit records this requirement as missing because the timeline is two narratives with no non-narrative state event. The progression lives in the engine's four order refusals, and the position of the bridge inside the chain is the argument: a vasopressor recorded before the phenotype is a guess about a heart nobody has looked at, and a device escalated before the culprit vessel is opened is treating the consequence of an artery that is still shut. Recognition precedes the phenotype review, the phenotype precedes the bridge, the bridge precedes cause control, and cause control precedes the reassessment. Every refusal is exercised by a reference transcript.

Five declared decisions recognize the worsening hypoperfusion and activate experienced shock and catheterization help off the trajectory rather than a diagnosis; review the acute-MI cause, the left-sided congested phenotype and the immediate mechanical, rhythm, right-heart and noncardiac alternatives; record perfusion-linked vasopressor bridge intent without primary fluid loading; prioritize prompt culprit-vessel revascularization ahead of unselected device escalation or routine multivessel treatment; and reassess pressure, perfusion, congestion, rhythm, gas exchange and organ trajectory. The lesson examines nobody, acquires no monitoring or test, diagnoses nothing, delivers no oxygen or drug, obtains no access, selects no dose, images nothing, catheterizes, revascularizes, supports, transfers and dispositions nobody, and predicts no outcome.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The branch ends at a recorded trajectory reassessment on an authored response that improves. Later actions cannot restart an ended branch, and the ending is explicit that improvement at this point means the bridge is doing what a bridge does rather than that the shock is treated: the artery is the shock and it is not open yet. The revascularization decisions, the device questions, the shock team's work and the organ trajectory all stay open.

Five observed-state prompts at version 0.1.0 read the learner's own recorded steps — one per recorded step, because this lesson has no unordered lane. The reflex it works against is the fluid, and the module now teaches both halves of that: a MAP of 58 with a rising lactate pulls hard towards a bolus, this patient's left ventricle is already failing into lungs full of B-lines, and the same instinct that is right in the septic-shock lesson is wrong here. The bridge beat says so directly and points at the other lesson, because the pair is the teaching. The recognition beat calls the MAP the least interesting number on the screen and gives the reason team activation is a step of its own: it takes time you do not have later, and it should happen off the trajectory rather than off a diagnosis. The phenotype beat treats the echo's negatives as the load-bearing part — a tamponade, a right-ventricular infarct, an acute severe mitral regurgitation or a ruptured septum each make this a different emergency, and two of them need a surgeon rather than a vasopressor. The cause beat explains why support layered onto an artery that is still shut is expensive, invasive and not the fix. The reassessment beat refuses to let improvement close anything, because the artery is the shock. Worked example 0.1.0 drives the ordinary controls through the real engine to the reassessment, and its narration is generated from the tutor's own prose so the two cannot drift apart. A test asserts that no beat anywhere names a vasopressor dose, a pressure target, a device, or a fluid volume. tests/unit/cardiogenic-shock-worked-example.test.ts verifies every beat and every refusal against the real engine, and tests/ui/critical-care-cardiogenic-shock.test.tsx verifies the tray, silence when unassisted, stable controls while watching, and version binding.

src/modules/anesthesia/ui/Debrief.tsx maps all five objectives to accepted engine events; the no-action path meets none and the expert path meets all five. The counterfactual is the one a low pressure invites: the common-error path recognises the shock and reaches straight for the bridge without looking at the heart — a vasopressor chosen for a phenotype nobody has established — and meets one of five, because the engine gates the bridge behind the phenotype review and everything after it becomes unavailable. The recovery path reviews the phenotype before the shock has been named and is refused, reaches for cause control before the bridge that holds him through it and is refused again, and still completes from the same positions.

Five observed-state prompts at version 0.1.0 read the learner's own recorded steps — one per recorded step, because this lesson has no unordered lane. The reflex it works against is the label, and the module builds that trap deliberately: septic shock taught one fluid decision, cardiogenic shock taught the opposite, and this patient is both, so the pull is to decide which one she really is and apply that lesson's answer. The recognition beat makes the mottled knees and the warm hands the finding rather than a contradiction to resolve, and gives the reason help is called before a label exists. The haemodynamics beat splits the panel explicitly — the ejection fraction of 25%, the cardiac index of 1.7 and the wedge of 24 describe a failing congested pump, while the SVR of 720 with a temperature of 39.1°C and a consolidated lobe describes vasodilation — and holds two cautions: those are suggested ranges rather than cutoffs, and she is already on vasoactive support, which changes what every number means. The support beat excludes blind fluid loading with a wedge of 24 and B-lines, and says the septic half does not change that. The causes beat names the failure it exists to prevent: having called the shock mixed, a team can treat the naming as the answer and let one pathway go unowned. The reassessment beat calls improvement here the easiest thing in the module to over-read. Worked example 0.1.0 drives the ordinary controls through the real engine to the reassessment, and its narration is generated from the tutor's own prose so the two cannot drift apart. Five observed-state prompts at version 0.1.0 read the learner's own recorded steps — one per recorded step, because this lesson has no unordered lane. The phenotype beat reads the two filling pressures against each other — 18 on the right and 10 on the left is where the congestion is and where it is not — and says the small left ventricle is small because the right one is not delivering to it rather than because she is dry, with the septal flattening as the same fact seen a second way. The support beat states plainly that neither reflex is forbidden as a matter of principle and that what is excluded is doing either automatically. The triggers beat notes that hypoxia and acidosis are both consequences of her state and causes of it worsening, and that restarting interrupted pulmonary-vascular therapy is a specialist decision rather than a resumption. Worked example 0.1.0 drives the ordinary controls through the real engine to the reassessment and asks the tutor for its narration rather than storing a copy. massive-pe-fixtures.ts binds seed 8933 and content 0.1.0 to expert, straight-to-the-bridge error, recovery, and no-action paths. The imaging-confirmed saddle pulmonary embolism in an intubated patient still hypotensive despite reported parenteral anticoagulation and three vasoactive infusions, the MAP of 50 mmHg with HR 132/min, capillary refill 6 seconds, mottled cool extremities, no command following, urine 5 mL/h and a lactate rising from 5.2 to 8.1 mmol/L, the 82% on FiO2 1.0 with continuous capnography and reported bilateral ventilation, the fixed CT reporting acute central pulmonary emboli, and the fixed echo reporting severe RV dilation and hypokinesis, septal flattening, a small LV, no effusion, no tension pneumothorax and no active external bleeding pattern are authored constants; no thrombus, ECMO or reperfusion model is claimed, and no outcome follows from any choice. tests/integration/massive-pe-runs.test.ts replays every path frame-for-frame across all three guidance levels and both practice regions.

The shared audit records this requirement as missing because the timeline is two narratives with no non-narrative state event. The progression lives in the engine's four order refusals, and this chain is deliberately short-tempered because the patient is the sickest in the module: the rescue teams are activated in step one, before the imaging review, since the diagnosis is already made and repeating it costs him time. What the later refusals protect is the distinction the lesson turns on — a bridge that supports his circulation is not treatment of his clot — by keeping the support review and the bridge activation in separate steps so neither can stand in for the other. Every refusal is exercised by a reference transcript.

Five declared decisions recognize refractory PE shock and activate PERT plus ECMO-capable rescue; integrate the fixed PE, RV, ventilation, perfusion and alternate-cause findings without delaying rescue for repeated diagnosis and while keeping bleeding risk visible; record RV-sensitive perfusion, oxygenation, ventilation, rhythm and anticoagulation review without blind fluid loading; activate resource- and candidacy-dependent VA-ECMO as a stabilization bridge rather than clot treatment or a universal device rule; and reassess perfusion and oxygenation after the authored bridge while individualizing any additional reperfusion strategy. The lesson examines nobody, acquires or interprets no monitoring, CT, echo, laboratory or haemodynamic data, diagnoses nothing, delivers no oxygen, ventilation, anticoagulation, fluid or drug, obtains no access, selects no dose, performs no CPR, cannulation, ECMO, thrombectomy, thrombolysis or embolectomy, transfers and dispositions nobody, and predicts no outcome.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The branch ends at a recorded trajectory reassessment on an authored bridge response that improves. Later actions cannot restart an ended branch, and the ending is explicit about what the improvement is: a circulation being carried rather than a clot being treated, with the obstruction exactly where it was. Whether any additional advanced reperfusion is warranted stays open, because its usefulness in a patient already on VA-ECMO is not established — so neither doing it nor withholding it is the automatic answer, and no thrombus resolution, adjunctive benefit or outcome is claimed.

Five observed-state prompts at version 0.1.0 read the learner's own recorded steps — one per recorded step, because this lesson has no unordered lane. The first reflex it works against is the urge to keep diagnosing: everything about this patient invites another study, and the diagnosis is already in his notes, so the pattern beat is explicit that the most expensive thing anybody could do now is order another one to be sure. The recognition beat justifies why team activation comes before the review — the people who can help take time to assemble and he has none — and names the category without hiding behind it. The support beat sharpens the fluid argument the previous lesson made: this ventricle is obstructed at its outflow, so volume distends the one chamber keeping him alive, and it adds the ventilation point, that the pressures which recruit a lung are the pressures that raise the afterload he is failing against. The bridge beat is where the lesson's real claim sits: VA-ECMO takes over the circulation the obstruction defeated and does not touch the clot, and it is resource- and candidacy-dependent rather than a rule. The reassessment beat says the improvement is a circulation being carried rather than a clot being treated, and notes that this is the moment the distinction is easiest to lose. Worked example 0.1.0 drives the ordinary controls through the real engine to the reassessment and asks the tutor for its narration rather than storing a copy. A test asserts that no beat anywhere cannulates, names a dose or an anticoagulant, or claims the clot has been treated. tests/unit/massive-pe-worked-example.test.ts verifies every beat and every refusal against the real engine, and tests/ui/critical-care-massive-pe.test.tsx verifies the tray, silence when unassisted, stable controls while watching, and version binding.

septic-shock-resuscitation-fixtures.ts binds seed 5821 and content 0.1.0 to expert, straight-to-the-plan error, recovery, and no-action paths. The two hours since probable ascending cholangitis was recognised, the reported blood cultures, empiric antimicrobials, 2,100 mL of balanced crystalloid at 30 mL/kg and running norepinephrine, the physiology at MAP 64 mmHg, HR 118/min, refill 5 seconds, mottling to the knees, urine 12 mL/h, reduced attention and a lactate risen from 5.8 to 6.4 mmol/L, the passive-leg-raise panel moving stroke volume from 48 to 49 mL, the diffuse B-lines, the undone biliary source control, and the fixed 10-minute response at MAP 68 mmHg with unchanged urine and an unrepeated lactate are authored constants; no hemodynamic, fluid-kinetic or antimicrobial model is claimed, and no outcome follows from any choice. tests/integration/septic-shock-resuscitation-runs.test.ts replays every path frame-for-frame across all three guidance levels and both practice regions.

The shared audit records this requirement as missing because the timeline is two narratives with no non-narrative state event. Nothing about this patient changes on a clock; what changes is what the learner has established, and the progression is a strict five-step chain in the engine's refusals with no unordered lane and no time gate. The chain is the argument: the prior claims are separated from the present response before the perfusion is read, the perfusion is read before fluid responsiveness is tested, and the dynamic test lands before any plan is recorded. A learner reaching for another bolus finds two steps in the way. Every refusal is exercised by a reference transcript.

Five declared decisions reconcile the prior antimicrobial, fluid, vasopressor and source-control intents with what was reported delivered and what response is actually present; reassess pressure alongside brain, skin, kidney, lactate and respiratory tolerance so the MAP is one signal rather than proof; use the fixed dynamic response and lung findings to constrain further fluid; activate individualized hemodynamic support and urgent biliary source control in parallel; and reassess multi-organ perfusion and unresolved shock. The lesson examines nobody, measures, samples, scans or calculates nothing, diagnoses nothing, prescribes or delivers no fluid or drug, adjusts no device, performs no drainage, determines no disposition or prognosis, and predicts no outcome — and it offers no control that would give a blind repeat bolus, which is the single action the scenario exists to prevent.
The scenario executes through the shared deterministic anesthesia engine rather than a display-only script.

The branch ends at a recorded trajectory reassessment on an authored 10-minute response in which the pressure and rate have moved a little, the urine output has not moved at all, and the lactate has not been rechecked. Later actions cannot restart an ended branch, and the ending certifies passiveLegRaiseStrokeVolumeChangePercent at a fixed 2 with blindRepeatFluidOffered false. Persistent hypoperfusion, source control, support requirements, alternate causes, organ failure, durability and outcome all stay explicitly open: this is a patient still in shock, and reading the ending as a response would be reading two figures out of eight.

Five observed-state prompts at version 0.1.0 read the learner's own recorded steps — one per recorded step, because this lesson has no unordered lane and so no state where the tutor has to name a choice. The reflex it works against is the next bolus: everything about this patient argues for more fluid, and the fixed dynamic panel says another litre goes into her lungs rather than her circulation. The context beat separates the three things a resuscitation record blurs — what was ordered, what was reported delivered, and what response is present — and says why that matters: it is how a team ends up believing a patient has had treatment she has not had, or has responded to treatment she has. The perfusion beat counts six signals and observes that five of them describe a patient who is not perfusing while the sixth is the one a MAP target invites you to fix. The fluid beat pairs the two per cent stroke-volume change with the new B-lines as two halves of one sentence, and marks both as her facts rather than universal cutoffs. The plan beat gives the reason source control is the half that changes her outcome: an obstructed infected biliary tree does not respond to a better vasopressor plan, and antimicrobials cannot reach what is not draining. The trajectory beat refuses to call a four-millimetre pressure rise a response when the kidney has not moved and the lactate has not been rechecked. Worked example 0.1.0 drives the ordinary controls through the real engine to the reassessment, and its narration is generated from the tutor's own prose so the two cannot drift apart. A test asserts that no beat anywhere names a fluid volume, a pressure target, a vasopressor dose, or a drainage procedure. tests/unit/septic-shock-resuscitation-worked-example.test.ts verifies every beat and every refusal against the real engine, and tests/ui/critical-care-septic-shock-resuscitation.test.tsx verifies the tray, silence when unassisted, stable controls while watching, and version binding.

src/modules/anesthesia/ui/Debrief.tsx maps all five objectives to accepted engine events; the no-action path meets none and the expert path meets all five. The counterfactual is the one the patient's appearance invites: the common-error path reconciles the prior claims and then goes straight to the plan, skipping the perfusion review and the dynamic test — the sequence that ends in another bolus — and meets one of five, because the engine gates the plan behind both. The recovery path attempts the perfusion review before the claims have been separated and is refused, attempts the dynamic test before the perfusion review and is refused again, and still completes from the same positions.
